verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both clauses are stated, in two pieces each. First clause: Lean fixes the paper's unnamed c to 1/4 (exp(-(1/(4·lam)))), and splits the C¹_η norm into a value bound (`pulse_coefficients_exp_bound`, with 1 + |amp η| on the right) and an η-derivative bound obtained from `pulse_coefficients_hasDerivAt` composed with `affineCoefficients_exp_bound`, whose right-hand side is |1 + 3η²| + |amp'| rather than 1 + |Amp|; that is exactly the paper's own gloss two lines below the display ("the affine coefficients of 1 and Amp have the stated parameter bounds"). `paper_correction_bounds` packages the same estimate for the correction itself at every fixed radial derivative order k, matching "Every fixed y derivative satisfies the same estimate". Second clause: `exact_axial_moments` gives M = J = 0 at c.endpoint = c.pulseStart + 13/c.lam, and `massMoment_after_pulse`/`angularMoment_after_pulse` extend it to all y ≥ endpoint, i.e. "after the pulse".
